findings.headline: People ask to be shown what fits, pockets and how the bag carries
saw: Shoppers ask what a bag actually takes in a normal day. Commenters name pockets, laptop space, water bottle holders, luggage pass through, size differences between models and the features included.
Buyers ask to see the bag in use, not only named. People also ask for the missing shopping basics, such as brand, price, buying links and adjustable parts.
findings.means: People do not treat function as a list on a spec card. Comments want the bag turned into a visible shopping decision, what it carries, how it is organised, and how it sits on a body in work, school and travel terms. The missing basics around price and where to buy sit in the same picture.
practice: Buyers frame one bag against work, school and travel, not one setting.
Commenters ask for carry comfort and pocket layout alongside brand, price and links.

sections.title: Where the confusion starts

items.title: Style test
items.text: People doubt that a bag in this space will look stylish, feel convenient to carry, or meet a premium aesthetic.

sections.lead: Buyers do not read bags in this space as practical objects alone. Comments test them against style, carry convenience and a premium look.
sections.note: Confusion starts when a bag in this space is read through fashion and everyday use expectations at the same time.
